free_tier.stated: E2B Desktop runs on the E2B Sandbox plan: Hobby is USD 0 a month with a one-time USD 100 in usage credits, up to 10 concurrently running sandboxes and up to 1 hour of continuous runtime per sandbox; no credit card is required to start, though some accounts are asked to verify with a one-time USD 5 card payment.
free_tier.notes: The SDK docs state the Desktop Sandbox is built on top of E2B Sandbox, so the same account, credits and per-second CPU/RAM rates apply; no separate Desktop price is published.

per_object_cap.stated: The desktop sandbox is an Ubuntu 22.04 environment with an XFCE desktop; a create example sets resolution 1024x720 at 96 dpi. The E2B plan table states up to 8 vCPUs and 10 GiB of sandbox disk on Hobby, with 1 to 8 vCPUs and 1 to 8 GiB of RAM configurable.

retention.stated: Paused sandbox retention is unlimited on every plan: a paused sandbox keeps its filesystem and memory with no time-to-live and no automatic deletion; the default timeout is 5 minutes and on timeout the sandbox is killed unless onTimeout is set to pause.

egress.terms: No egress charge or allowance is stated; the pricing page bills CPU and RAM per second and states sandbox disk is included at no extra cost.

interface_detail: The @e2b/desktop (npm) and e2b-desktop (pip) SDKs expose mouse, keyboard, screenshot and VNC streaming on a Linux desktop; E2B Surf is an open-source computer-use agent using it.
tooling: npm i @e2b/desktop or pip install e2b-desktop; sandbox.stream.start() gives a browser-viewable VNC URL; E2B provides Python, JavaScript and TypeScript SDKs and a CLI.
chaining: The desktop sandbox shares one E2B account and its USD 100 credits with the ordinary code sandbox, so an agent can switch between shell work and computer use while drawing on the same one-time balance.

limits.value: 1 hour maximum continuous runtime per sandbox on the Hobby plan; 24 hours on Pro
USD 100 one-time usage credit on Hobby; vCPU USD 0.000014 per vCPU-second and RAM USD 0.0000045 per GiB-second
with no payment method on file, every project in the workspace is blocked shortly after the credits are spent

limits_note: Continuous runtime resets on pause and resume; a paused sandbox is not billed and does not count toward the concurrency limit.
binding_note: The Hobby one-hour continuous runtime cap ends a desktop session first at sustained use; the USD 100 credit is one-time and larger, and pausing resets the clock.

identity_cost.detail: The E2B console sign-up page renders 'Sign up with your email and a password or a social provider' with E-Mail, Name and Password fields; the pricing page states 'No credit card required to start', with an optional one-time USD 5 card verification for some accounts that is added to project credits.

reliability_note: The default timeout is 5 minutes and the default on-timeout action is kill, which loses in-memory state; a stream may drop after about an hour because of load-balancer drains even while the sandbox keeps running, so clients reconnect.
confidence_note: The Desktop SDK, its dependence on E2B Sandbox and the computer-use flow are quoted from the vendor docs and PyPI page read on 2026-11-25; prices, limits and signup gate are from the vendor pricing and billing pages on the same date.

notes: E2B Desktop is a graphical variant of the same hosted E2B Sandbox, not a separately priced product: its SDK creates a desktop sandbox with mouse, keyboard, screenshot and VNC streaming against the same API key and the same USD 100 one-time Hobby credit. At the default 2 vCPU / 4 GiB shape the published rates give USD 0.1656 per running hour, so the credit buys about 604 one-hour-or-shorter sessions. Hobby caps each session at one hour of continuous runtime; pausing resets it and is free. The existing compute/e2b record covers the same plan for code sandboxes; this record is the desktop computer-use tier.
